tab: HW Line Items, data rows 15 to 52928
method: Rules are numbered and tested in number order; the first rule whose match is true captures the line, and no line is tested against a later rule, so every line maps through exactly one rule. Each rule states the match in column terms, the destination taken only from the operating model structure, and the lines and dollars it captures. Every rule was re-derived from the words of its match alone, in a second implementation, and returns the lines and dollars it claims, zero exceptions. Rules whose destination is not decided by the source carry an open question instead of a portfolio and platform. The grammar follows the adjudicated convention: the cost centre in column C decides, except in APPLH_INFOTECH, which pools technology spend for every portfolio and where the product named in column N decides; a line that recharges a product out of that centre into a named centre takes the destination of the centre that receives it. Inside a cost centre that spans several businesses and names none, the bulk fuels code, the product or system named in the line decides, and lines naming none are open. Rule 47 is appended after rule 46 and is named out of rule 43 in that rule's own match, so the stated matches partition the block in any order of application. Columns used: C cost centre, D cost centre name, E cost element, I auxiliary account assignment (internal order), K vendor, L purchase order, N document text.
basis_scope: The 2026 Budget tab of the same file covers 35 technology cost centres and its scope on the line item tabs is cost centre APPLH_INFOTECH. It is cited only on rules whose lines sit in that centre, rules 37, 38, 41, 48 and 49, and there as corroboration after the column fact, at sheet rows 156, 262 and 264 for the two rules added in the fourth issue. Question Q1 quotes the tab to show a conflict between two conventions inside the file, not to place a line.

Consuming centre: the same tab maps cost centre ITSDM_C, IT Recharge Costs SDM, cost element 800993 Corp Oncharge Retail, minus 1,237,800, to Ampol Retail / Network/QSR, and the 784 mapping values present on the SW tab carry the portfolio of the cost centre that holds the spend.

open_questions.name: Blue Yonder prepaid account journals
open_questions.question: Which invoices do the prepaid references release?
open_questions.missing_fact: Which invoices the prepaid references 5013501007, 5013501085, 5013498113 and 5013491723 release.
open_questions.reasoning: Stays an open question. The arithmetic is real and exact: H31372 at -2,110,731.33 is eleven twelfths of H31369, "BY SAAS CLOUD AGREEMENT 2025/2026", 2,302,616.00, and H31371 at -85,315.08 is eleven twelfths of H31368, "BY SAAS DAS (REPLICATION DB) ENVIRONMENT", 93,071.00; both invoices are the only lines in either tab carrying those amounts, both sit in the same cost centre APPLMTOTAL, the same cost element 801430 and the same month as the journal, and each has a monthly stream at exactly one twelfth, 191,884.67 and 7,755.92, running from the following month on shared CO documents. It still fails the acceptance test, on four checkable grounds. One, the journal names no product: column N reads only "MOVE TO PREPAID ACCOUNT.REF 5013501085" and column K is Not assigned, so the charged business unit cannot verify the charge from the named columns. Two, the reference numbers 5013501007 and 5013501085 appear on no other line of either tab, so a reviewer following the only identifier the journal carries reaches nothing. Three, the cost centre and cost element cannot stand in for the missing product name, because the 430 lines at APPLMTOTAL and 801430 split three ways under the block's own rules, 6,250,739.60 to Ampol Retail / Store Operations, 78,626.43 to Ampol Retail / Network/QSR and 352,784.18 to TDD / TDD. Four, the eleven twelfths relationship is not a convention operating in this file: the same CO document 5116660265 carries two further legs formed identically, S11648 at -67,008.00 and S12062 at -387,189.69, and neither has any counterparty at twelve elevenths, one eleventh or one twelfth anywhere in either tab, so the arithmetic succeeds on two of the four legs of the one document it is drawn from. Every other prepaid journal in the file names its product in column N (PREPAY CORNTERSTONE RENEWAL, SALESFORCE JAN-DEC 26 PREPAY, MOVE D365 LICENSE (JUN26-MAY27) TO PREPAYMENTS, DIEBOLD FUELPAY FILLING SAAS JAN - JUNE 26 PREPAID); these four are the only ones that do not. Blue Yonder is named on no line of the 2026 Budget tab, so there is no corroboration there either. Written as a rule it would place -2,196,046.41 on a business unit that cannot check it, on an inference the file itself does not repeat.
open_questions.source_of_reasoning: Adversarial verification, prepaid_verdict in qa_b1_findings.json, recorded verbatim.
open_questions.note_on_the_quoted_split: The three way split quoted in ground three was computed against the first issue of this file. In this issue the same 430 lines at APPLMTOTAL and cost element 801430 split 6,302,871.91 to Ampol Retail / Store Operations, 26,494.12 to Ampol Retail / Network/QSR and 352,784.18 to TDD / TDD, with 368.98 open under Q4 and the two journals themselves open here. The ground holds: the centre and the cost element still split three ways.

notes: Every destination is spelled as the structure document spells it. Where the 2026 Budget tab words the same destination differently, Finance / AU Finance and Fuel Infrastructure / Manufacturing & Group Projects, the difference is wording only and is left for alignment at integration.

No rule contradicts the mapping values present in the source file. The only leaf centre in this block that carries such values is APPLLUBRICANTS, where all 125 rows on the SW tab read B2B & Energy Solutions / B2B; rule 17 places that centre on the same pair.
Leaf total ties the export's own result row: 39,772 lines, 25,468,998.32. Ruled 20,834,690.50 over 1,565 lines plus open 4,634,307.82 over 38,207 lines re-adds to 25,468,998.32 to the cent.

Cost centre APPLSIG_ITEMS is a leaf on this tab, unlike the SW tab where it is a parent. Of its 11,975,400.23, the amount of 11,897,067.66 on cost element 801440 is the POS programme transferred to the significant item CRPOSSIG, whose cost centre name in the same export is CONV RETAIL POS, and 74,923.11 is device catalogue billing; it is not a device fleet.

The POS programme appears three times over: gross charges on internal order E.25.002 in the marketing operating centre (rule 7, 11,349,211.57), the monthly transfer out of that centre and into the significant items centre (rule 8, both sides, 457,360.72 net because two transfer documents carry no marketing side), and lines naming the programme outside the order (rule 11, 68,403.67). The four AmPOS rules together place 11,874,975.96 on Ampol Retail / AmPOS, all flagged significant item funded.

Document 5118145663, the Snowflake transfer to CRPOSSIG, is captured by rule 8 with the other transfers. The cost centre decides, so the leg on this tab takes the rule of the centre that holds it, and the leg of the same document on the SW tab sits in the same portfolio under the rule of its own centre. The product named remains visible in column N for any later platform ruling.

Product families are billed into the bulk fuels cost centre as well as into the centre that owns each family: Blue Yonder support 7,122.84, store field services 179,987.22, POS vendor support 43,319.50, forecourt dispenser service 865.50, outdoor payment terminals 17,932.58, payment gateway fees 1,767.08 and workforce management support 146.94, all ruled to Ampol Retail, and network outsourcing 115,424.13 ruled to TDD. The bulk fuels code names no single business, so the product named in the line decides those lines; every bulk fuels line that names no product is open under question Q3.

Platform placements inside Ampol Retail rest on what column N names: point of sale, back office, forecourt dispensers, payment terminals, self checkout and store field services are the store estate; site connectivity and the quick service restaurant network are the site network; the POS replacement programme is the project platform. Rule 23 moved from Above Store to Store Operations in this issue because the store back office system runs inside the store and the reading that placed it above the store rested on a tab that does not contain this cost centre.

Lines from vendor AMPOL MANAGEMENT (USD) SERVICES PTE carrying the text "IT RELATED EXPENDITURE" follow the cost centre that holds each line, so the lines land in three places: technology centre 494.78 ruled to TDD / TDD, bulk fuels 4,622.95 open under Q3, significant items 109.62 open under Q5.

Rule 19 captures both sides of the operational technology recharges, the charge in the bulk fuels centre and the matching credit in the technology centre, so the pair nets in Commercial Fuels / Supply at minus 27,986.92 rather than resting in two portfolios.

Three rules capture both sides of a pair posted inside one CO document, so each pair rests in one place: rule 8 (POS transfers, credit in the marketing centre and debit in the significant items centre), rule 10 (the transfer to HSPECIAL) and rule 19 (operational technology recharges). Rule 9 captures four such pairs and holds the eight lines open. One pair is split by design and is listed in contra_documents: CO document 5117738696, where the significant items leg is ruled and the pooled technology leg is held open, each following what its own centre routes by.

The device catalogue is billed on cost element 801450 in exactly fourteen leaf cost centres: APPLBULKFUEL 2,236,563.61, APPLFIREFINING 2,194,440.75, APPLMTOTAL 784,976.61, APPLHFIN 455,830.58, APPLAETOTAL 339,213.22, APPLHHR 301,508.63, APPLLUBRICANTS 167,785.00, APPLBRNDCOMS 95,697.19, APPLSIG_ITEMS 75,883.11, APPLHLSA 54,667.53, APPLHALT 42,825.15, APPLH_INFOTECH 22,216.43, APPLRCALSTORES 3,790.00, APPLGENERAL 1,200.00. Rule 9 adds the eight reallocation lines on top of those figures, 480.00 in APPLAETOTAL, 480.00 in APPLH_INFOTECH and minus 960.00 in APPLSIG_ITEMS.

Three leaf cost centres resolve entirely into open question Q1 because every line each one holds is device catalogue billing: APPLHLSA 54,667.53, APPLHALT 42,825.15 and APPLGENERAL 1,200.00. APPLRCALSTORES resolves the same way apart from one tablet subscription of 18.09.

Significant item spend sitting in open entries, for any integration step that carries the flag: cost centre APPLSIG_ITEMS holds 75,883.11 under rule 1, minus 720.00 under rule 4, minus 960.00 under rule 9 and 109.62 under rule 46. Rule 50 carries the significant item flag on the 3,903.32 it rules.
Cost element 801445 Network-SecurID Card carries only seven lines, 1,977.34, all in the bulk fuels centre; the SecurID label does not describe the lines and the document text is site security work.
Raw rows are untouched: no row was reshaped, no value edited, and every line keeps its export row number as its identifier (H15 is HW row 15).
